prompt: Each input line is an RFC-2822 date: 'Wkd, DD Mon YYYY HH:MM:SS +HHMM' (weekday name is decoration and must be ignored). Convert each line to UTC ISO-8601 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ', one per output line, same order. Output only the converted datetimes.
notes: Held-out: email-style dates; combines weekday-ignoring with offset arithmetic from A-EXP-02.

prompt: Each input line is an ISO week date 'YYYY-Www-d' (week 01-53, weekday 1=Monday..7=Sunday). Convert each line to the calendar date YYYY-MM-DD, one per output line, same order. Output only the dates.
notes: Held-out: ISO week arithmetic including a 53-week year (2020).

prompt: Parse the input as semicolon-delimited data (delimiter ';', double-quote quoting, first row is the header; commas inside fields are literal). Output a JSON array of objects mapping header names to field values (all values strings, row order preserved). Output only the JSON.
notes: Held-out: non-comma delimiter; commas must NOT split fields.

prompt: Parse the input as CSV (RFC 4180: comma delimiter, double-quote quoting), except: lines starting with '#' are comments and blank lines are ignored; the first remaining line is the header. Output a JSON array of objects (all values strings, row order preserved). Output only the JSON.
notes: Held-out: comment/blank-line skipping layered on CSV parsing.

prompt: The input is two lines, each a JSON object (base, then patch). Deep-merge them: the patch wins on conflicts; nested objects merge recursively; arrays and all other values are replaced wholesale. Output the merged object. Output only the JSON.
notes: Held-out: recursive merge with array-replace semantics.

prompt: The input is one JSON address object with keys street, city, zip or postal, country or cc. Output {"street":...,"city":...,"postal":...,"country":...} where street/city are trimmed, postal is uppercased with all spaces removed, and country is the uppercased 2-letter code. Output only the JSON.
notes: Held-out: address normalization with key aliases and postal cleanup.

prompt: Parse one BSD syslog line: '<PRI>Mon DD HH:MM:SS host tag[pid]: msg' (day may be space-padded). Output JSON {"pri":N,"time":"Mon D HH:MM:SS","host":...,"tag":...,"pid":N,"msg":...} with time day single-spaced. Output only the JSON.
notes: Held-out: syslog format with space-padded day and pri/tag/pid extraction.

prompt: Input lines are 'TS user event' where event is login, action, or logout and TS has no spaces. Group into sessions: each login opens a session for that user (in input order), later events attach to that user's open session, logout closes it. Output a JSON array in login order of {user, login, logout, actions} where logout is null when never closed and actions counts 'action' events. Output only the JSON.

checks.input:
2026-10-05T10:00:00Z alice login
2026-10-05T10:01:00Z alice action
2026-10-05T10:02:00Z bob login
2026-10-05T10:03:00Z alice logout

notes: Held-out: multi-line stateful sessionization; interleaved users in check 1.

prompt: Each input line is Unix epoch seconds (integer, may be negative for pre-1970). Convert each line to UTC ISO-8601 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ', one per output line, same order. Output only the converted datetimes.
notes: Held-out: raw integer epochs incl. a negative (pre-1970) value; no weekday/offset decoration unlike A-TRN-01.

prompt: Each input line is 'MM/DD/YYYY HH:MM:SS AM|PM' in US Eastern Standard Time (UTC-5; all dates are January so no daylight saving applies). Convert each line to UTC ISO-8601 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ', one per output line, same order. Output only the converted datetimes.
notes: Held-out: 12-hour clock plus named-zone offset in one step; midnight/noon meridiem edges included.

prompt: Input is tab-separated values: first line is the header, fields may be double-quoted (quotes may contain literal tabs). Output a JSON array of objects, one per data row, keys from the header. Output only the JSON.
notes: Held-out: tab delimiter with quoted-tab fields; goes beyond semicolon/comment variants in TRN-03/04.

prompt: Input is pipe-separated values: first line is the header. A backslash escapes the next character (\| is a literal pipe, \\ is a literal backslash). Output a JSON array of objects, one per data row. Output only the JSON.
notes: Held-out: backslash-escape discipline instead of quoting; the escape char itself appears in check 2.

prompt: Input is one flat JSON object whose keys are dot paths (e.g. {"a.b": 1}). Output the nested JSON object it denotes. Output only the JSON.
notes: Held-out: inverse direction of the flatten tasks in exposure; shared-prefix merging required.

prompt: Input is a JSON array of objects, each with a "status" string field. Output one JSON object mapping each distinct status to its count. Output only the JSON.
notes: Held-out: aggregation over records (group-by-count); exposure aggregates logs, never record arrays.

prompt: Each input line is an Apache combined log line. Output a JSON array with one object per line: {"host", "user", "method", "path", "status" (number), "bytes" (number, 0 when the field is '-')}. A '-' user means absent: emit null. Ignore ident, timestamp, referrer, and user-agent. Output only the JSON.
notes: Held-out: combined format with quoted request plus two trailing quoted fields; '-' byte counts included.

prompt: Input is one line of space-separated key=value pairs; values may be single- or double-quoted and quoted values may contain spaces and '='. Output one JSON object of the pairs (quotes removed). Output only the JSON.
notes: Held-out: quoted values with interior spaces and '='; naive whitespace splitting fails.
